sections.title: ENGINEERING BASELINE
sections.exactContract:
15 / ENGINEERING BASELINE
System architecture and technology
Use a modular monolith with a separate background worker, not an early microservices estate. The web application owns business logic and transactional boundaries; the worker executes durable exports, reminders, reconciliation and AI tasks. Public guidance and paid-document workflows should continue independently when optional services fail.
LAYER | PROPOSED IMPLEMENTATION | REASON / CONDITION
Web and API | Next.js + TypeScript on a supported Node.js release; Tailwind and accessible component primitives. | Server-rendered public content, one same-origin app/API and a typed codebase. Validate self-hosting. [S14]
Database | Managed PostgreSQL; Drizzle ORM with reviewed SQL migrations. | Relational integrity for tenants, content versions, assessments and purchases. Replit DB is preferred only after migration/backup proof. [S12]
Identity | Clerk managed customer authentication; application-owned workspace memberships and permissions. | Avoid custom passwords; do not confuse authentication with authorisation. [S15]
Files | Private Replit App Storage behind a storage adapter. | Access control, deletion, backup and worker credentials must pass the foundation spike. [S13]
Jobs | pg-boss in PostgreSQL; dedicated worker deployment. | Durable jobs without adding Redis initially; prove schema/privilege compatibility. [S21]
Documents | Canonical JSON → docx library and controlled HTML → Playwright/Chromium PDF. | One content revision, two tested formats; no arbitrary uploaded HTML. [S22–S23]
Commerce / messaging | Paystack hosted checkout; a verified transactional-email provider selected at Gate G0. | Server verification and observable message delivery; provider credentials remain server-side. [S16–S17]
AI | Server-side model adapter for customer drafting and a separately scoped editorial queue. | Separate draft/review configurations and gated publisher; select providers through quality, privacy and cost checks. [S18]
Observability | Structured application logs, metrics, error tracking and external uptime probes. | Redact document content; alert on user-impacting failures and security events.

Logical flow
Browser → HTTPS web/API → identity and authorisation → domain services → PostgreSQL / private object storage. Domain events → durable job queue → worker → renderer, email provider, PSP verification or AI adapter. Staff use the same controlled API through an independently permissioned admin interface.
Pin actual package/runtime versions after the technical spike. Record architecture decisions, licence compatibility and patch ownership. Keep interfaces replaceable. Drafting and reviewing may use separate configurations through one adapter; a second model/provider is optional and requires evaluation, cost and privacy checks.

sections.title: REPLIT PRODUCTION DESIGN
sections.exactContract:
16 / REPLIT PRODUCTION DESIGN
Deployment, environments and build controls
OPS-001  Separated environments  [R1 · Must] Use development, staging and production with distinct databases, storage namespaces/buckets, identity instances, PSP modes and secrets. Accept: no live personal data is seeded into dev; integration tests cannot charge production accounts.
OPS-002  Request and worker separation  [R1 · Must] Propose Replit Autoscale for the web/API and a Reserved VM for the queue worker. Accept: export, reminder and reconciliation jobs survive web-app scale-down and worker restarts. Deployment behaviour must be proven, not assumed. [S10–S11]
OPS-003  Controlled schema deployment  [R1 · Must] Review migration SQL and test against a production-shaped staging database. Replit’s documented schema publishing has limits for functions, grants and other objects, so validate ORM and queue migrations explicitly. Accept: one authorised migration owner; no competing automatic schema-push paths. [S12]
OPS-004  Secrets and account ownership  [R1 · Must] Keep secrets in environment-specific secret stores and managed provider accounts owned by Valo. Accept: no keys in prompts, browser bundles, commits or screenshots; rotation and emergency revocation are rehearsed.
OPS-005  Supply-chain and code review  [R1 · Must] Use a private Git repository, protected main branch, CI checks, dependency/secret scans and human approval for sensitive changes. Accept: the release identifies commit, migration, content/rule versions and known issues.
OPS-006  Hosting and data geography  [R1 · Must] Record actual hosting and processor regions before live data. Replit documentation describes US hosting by default and an enterprise EU request option; obtain the relevant transfer assessment and contracts. Accept: no claim that Nigerian customer data stays in Nigeria without proof. [S10]
OPS-007  Production compatibility spike  [R1 · Must] Prove identity callbacks, private storage, background queue, browser binaries, DB connection limits, backup/restore, domains and outbound provider calls. Accept: failures produce an approved architecture change before core implementation scales.
OPS-008  Safe rollback  [R1 · Must] Use backward-compatible database changes, versioned assets and reversible feature flags. Accept: deploy the previous application version safely or restore through a tested recovery plan; irreversible migrations require a separate approved runbook.
Controls for AI-assisted development
Coding agents may propose code, tests and migrations in development branches; they cannot enable live payments, remove production data, grant privileges or approve their own security work. The separately permissioned editorial pipeline may publish eligible content under EDP-001–012. Human owners approve sensitive platform deployments; content publication does not require human sign-off per item.
Changing from the proposed stack is allowed through an architecture decision record that preserves the same functional and acceptance requirements. Reusing a React/Vite demo is optional; do not rewrite working code solely to match a framework preference.

sections.title: PERSISTENT DOMAIN MODEL
sections.exactContract:
17 / PERSISTENT DOMAIN MODEL
Data model and integrity rules
ENTITY / RELATIONSHIP | MINIMUM FIELDS AND CONSTRAINTS
User → Membership → Workspace | Internal UUID; identity-provider ID unique; user/workspace unique membership; role/status; one owner minimum; workspace deletion state.
BusinessProfile → ProfileVersion | Workspace ID; legal form; registration/activity/location facts; unknown values; turnover metric/year; schema version; immutable version snapshot.
Template → TemplateVersion | Slug; category/licence/risk; immutable schema/content version; provenance/rights; AI-review manifest; scope, status, effective dates and object references.
Document → DocumentRevision | Workspace and creator; template version; structured content; revision number; change origin/manual or AI; optimistic-lock version; deletion state.
ExportJob → FileAsset | Workspace, document revision, format/render version; status/attempts; checksum, MIME type, size, private object key and retention date; idempotent key.
Authority / Jurisdiction / Source | Authority and jurisdiction; official URL; instrument/passage; effective dates; source snapshot/hash; fetched/AI-reviewed dates; availability and expiry.
Requirement → RequirementVersion | Applicability; source/claim links; effective interval; jurisdictions; actions/evidence; related templates; risk; AI-review manifest; next-check date.
RuleSet → RuleVersion | Validated conditions; requirement link; effective period; test-set hash; drafting/review run IDs; publication manifest; status and explanation.
Assessment → AssessmentItem | Workspace or short-lived anonymous context; profile version; rule-set version; as-of date; answer hash; results, reasons, gaps and source versions.
Task / Notification / Enquiry | Workspace/owner; origin assessment; user state/date; consent/preferences; delivery status/idempotent key; enquiry sharing permission and routing.
Product / Price / Order / Line | Immutable price snapshot; NGN/kobo totals; tax treatment; status; workspace; unique order reference; source product/licence version.
Payment / Event / Entitlement | Unique provider transaction/event IDs; raw-body hash; verified amounts; order; product/workspace grant; state; refund/dispute relation.
AuditEvent / Consent / Review | Actor type/ID; object/reason/time; terms version; model/prompt/run IDs; findings and claim map; exact content/source/policy hashes; immutable release decision.
Provider / Service / Booking | R1: consented verified profile + service; R2/R3: availability, quote, cancellation and settlement states. Do not activate future booking tables as live features.

Invariants that must be enforced
Every tenant-owned entity carries workspace_id. Use tenant-aware repository methods and composite foreign keys where needed to prevent cross-workspace references. Published content and assessment inputs are immutable versions. Money is integer minor units or fixed-precision decimal, never binary floats. UTC stores instants; date-only deadlines carry jurisdiction/timezone metadata. Unique constraints protect transaction references, entitlement grants and job idempotency.
Use database row-level security as defence in depth where supported and proved with least-privilege application roles; application authorisation remains mandatory. Index tenant foreign keys, publication/status, search vectors, dates and provider references. No generic “admin=true” client field may grant access.

sections.title: INTEGRATION DESIGN
sections.exactContract:
18 / INTEGRATION DESIGN
API contracts and transaction flows
INTERFACE | CONTRACT / AUTHORISATION
GET /api/v1/catalogue, /search | Public, approved records only; query/filter/cursor parameters; bounded page size; no master file objects.
GET/PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/:id/profile | Active workspace membership; PATCH includes expectedVersion; returns 409 on conflicting edits.
POST /api/v1/assessments | Typed profile answers or stored profileVersionId, asOfDate; returns assessmentId, rulesetVersion, recommendations and gaps.
POST/PATCH /api/v1/documents/:id | Owner permission and relevant template entitlement; structured field/content validation; revision-aware writes.
POST /api/v1/documents/:id/exports | format + revisionId + Idempotency-Key; returns 202 and jobId; worker revalidates resource access before delivery.
POST /api/v1/ai/drafts | Supported task, workspace/document context, schema version and allowed inputs; quota and privacy checks; 202 or bounded synchronous result.
POST /api/v1/orders / :id/checkout | Authenticated workspace buyer; server computes prices; stable order/reference and provider session; idempotent creation.
POST /api/v1/webhooks/paystack | Provider signature authentication, not browser session auth; raw body preserved; persist verified event; asynchronous idempotent processing.
POST /api/v1/enquiries /tasks | Authenticated owner for saved items; consented contact information; validation, abuse controls and durable confirmation.
POST /api/v1/admin/*/publish | Staff role + MFA, or scoped publisher credential; require valid hash-bound manifest, policy, source freshness and passing tests. No model-only approval bypass.

Response and failure conventions
Use JSON schema validation on requests and responses. Errors contain code, safe message, requestId and field-level details; never stack traces or secrets. Use 401 for missing identity, 403 for forbidden operations, 404 where existence should be concealed, 409 for revision conflicts, 422 for validation and 429 for quotas. Return a Retry-After hint where meaningful.
Payment fulfilment transaction
Validate event → persist the event uniquely → acknowledge → verify payment server-side → lock the order → compare amount/currency/reference → settle order and grant entitlement once → append receipt notification to the outbox → commit → dispatch notification. The callback uses the same idempotent fulfilment service. Refund/reversal events enter an audited compensating workflow, not a destructive rewrite. [S16–S17]
Document export transaction
Authorise → validate saved revision → insert/find unique export job → render from the immutable revision → write private object → atomically mark ready with checksum → send ready notification. Failed object writes never expose a “completed” export. Reconciliation removes orphaned temporary objects and retries safe failures.

sections.title: PERSONALISATION DETAIL
sections.exactContract:
19 / PERSONALISATION DETAIL
Rules, evidence and evaluation contract
Versioned rule specification
FIELD | EXPECTED REPRESENTATION
Identity and effectivity | ruleId; version; status; validFrom/validTo; sourceCheckedAt; aiReviewedAt; reviewBy; reviewManifestId; requirementVersionId.
Scope and predicates | Jurisdiction IDs; activity/legal-form constraints; all/any groups with allowlisted eq, in, exists, lt/lte/gt/gte operators; explicit unknown semantics.
Evidence | One or more approved source IDs with locators and applicable dates; typed thresholds with metric, currency, period and scope.
Output | Recommendation label; reason template; missing facts; next-step action; related template IDs; no invented statutory due date.
Test and audit linkage | Input/output fixtures with source locators; test results/hash; reason; draft/review run IDs; publication policy/manifest and prior version.

Evaluation sequence
Validate profile schema → select released rules valid for the assessment period → select evidence-supported jurisdiction/activity scope → evaluate true/false/unknown predicates → apply documented precedence → attach evidence → expose gaps → store a reproducible assessment. Held, expired or withdrawn rules cannot generate fresh definite recommendations.
A mismatch removes one recommendation, not all obligations. Missing facts, stale evidence or contradictory authorities create uncertainty. Only a source-supported precedence rule that passed the publication gates may suppress another item; an AI assertion or majority vote cannot establish legal hierarchy.
Illustrative test scenarios, not legal conclusions
PROFILE DIFFERENCE | EXPECTED PRODUCT BEHAVIOUR
Packaged-food activity vs software consultancy | Food profile uses source-backed AI-reviewed product/facility guidance; software profile is not sent there merely because it employs people. [S07]
Lagos vs an unchecked state/LGA | Use scoped Lagos content only for the Lagos context. Elsewhere show federal results plus a local-coverage gap, never copy Lagos fees.
Unknown turnover or band crossing a threshold | Ask for a suitable metric/year or state that applicability needs verification. Do not infer a tax exemption.
Employee count or activities change | Run the current approved rules and show a result comparison; preserve earlier assessments and user tasks.
Source superseded after an assessment | Flag affected recommendations and tasks; retain the original source/rule version for audit; do not pretend it was always current.

Production rules require retrieved authoritative evidence, separate AI validation and passing fixtures; these examples are not legal conclusions. The 80-scenario suite covers omissions, false positives, unknown facts and period boundaries. QA checks fixture provenance and execution; AI-produced expected answers alone are insufficient.

sections.title: OPERATING THE LIVE PRODUCT
sections.exactContract:
24 / OPERATING THE LIVE PRODUCT
Runbooks and launch readiness
Minimum runbook set
RUNBOOK | REQUIRED ACTIONS AND OWNER
Unavailable site / database | Engineering lead: detect, confirm impact, freeze risky changes, communicate, restore/rollback and validate critical journeys.
Payments or entitlement failure | Finance + engineering: reconcile PSP status, prevent duplicate collection, repair once through audited workflow, notify the affected buyer.
Broken export / AI outage | Engineering: isolate the failing feature, preserve draft, retry safely, provide manual/template fallback and assess cost impact.
Incorrect compliance content | Content owner + pipeline: suspend affected versions, recheck sources, identify impacted results, rerun gates, publish correction and notify when material.
Security or privacy incident | Incident lead + privacy owner: contain, revoke access, preserve evidence, assess source-backed notice requirements and record remediation.
Provider enquiry dispute | Support: acknowledge, check sharing consent and routing, set expectations and escalate; do not claim a booking that was never confirmed.
Deletion and recovery | Engineering + privacy owner: enforce retention, track legal holds, verify external deletion and reapply deletion events after a restore.

Commercial launch checklist
Approve business identity, domain ownership, PSP onboarding, prices, tax treatment, licences, terms/refunds and privacy notice. Use source-grounded AI checks for legal/tax wording; the product and finance/privacy owners accept their operational decisions. No specialist signature is a launch prerequisite. Resolve material evidence gaps or disable the affected activity before launch.
Confirm all R1 Must requirements and content floors; pass payment, tenant-isolation, accessibility and restore gates; perform a controlled live purchase/refund; verify transactional email authentication/delivery; confirm backup monitoring and staff MFA. Remove demo seeds, test credentials, “coming soon” primary CTAs, fake metrics and placeholder provider records.
Deployment sequence
Freeze scope → verify recoverable backup → approve migration/rollback → deploy staging candidate → obtain product/security operational sign-offs and passing AI content manifest → deploy approved build → run smoke tests → open limited traffic → monitor → expand only with healthy service and support. Subsequent eligible content updates publish automatically.
After release
Run daily payment reconciliation and error review; triage new content reports promptly. Review usage, support burden, source freshness, AI cost, conversion and retention weekly. Test a restore at least quarterly and after a major data/infrastructure change. Maintain a risk register and publish corrections without erasing historical evidence.
Business-hours support is the initial proposed staffing model; urgent security/payment monitoring still needs a named responder. No 24/7 human-support claim should appear unless it is actually staffed and funded.

sections.title: APPROVAL REQUIRED
sections.exactContract:
25 / APPROVAL REQUIRED
Open decisions, risks and handover
DECISION / OWNER | PROPOSED DEFAULT | DUE
D01 / Product owner | Approve R1/R2/R3 boundaries, one-business workspace and the 40-template content floor. | G0 / end W2
D02 / Technical lead + privacy owner | Confirm Replit deployment, storage/database restoration, identity provider and processor geography; approve any replacement adapter. | G0
D03 / Product + finance | Set prices, AI allowances, source-checked tax treatment, licence and refunds. Owner accepts terms; no counsel signature is assumed. | Before checkout testing; final before G4
D04 / Content lead | Configure AI editorial roles, publication policy, evidence gates, six deeper sectors and Lagos/FCT/Bayelsa source priorities; no specialist hiring dependency. | G0
D05 / Privacy owner | Approve data roles, transfer arrangements, retention, notice and rights/incident procedures. | Before live beta data
D06 / Product + delivery lead | Approve staffed capacity, operating spend cap and calendar; relative weeks are planning assumptions. | G0
D07 / Service operations | Decide whether R1 lists any providers; approve enquiry handling and future booking commercial model. | Before service pages go live

Principal build risks and treatments
AI content error or omission: use claim evidence, separate checks, blocked uncertain content and visible limitations. Broad scope: protect core journeys and defer expansion. Infrastructure mismatch: prove workers, migrations and recovery. Data/payment errors: isolation, idempotency and reconciliation. AI cost: measured queues and caps. Maintenance: fund source checks, correction handling and support.
Required handover package
Deliver repository/lockfile; schema/migrations; secret-free environment catalogue; deploy/restore runbooks; API schemas; architecture decisions; template rights; source snapshots and claim maps; rule fixtures; AI model/prompt versions, review findings and publication manifests; security/accessibility reports; privacy register; admin/support guide; known issues; ownership checklist; requirement-to-evidence matrix.
APPROVAL STANDARD  The product owner approves commercial scope and automation policy; the technical lead approves platform deployment/recovery; the AI publisher releases content that passes EDP gates. The privacy/security owner owns data risk. No per-item specialist or human content sign-off is required. A completion message alone never proves a gate passed.

Document control: baseline 1.1 revised 13 November 2026. Replaces specialist content sign-off with AI drafting, separate AI checks and automated publication gates. Requirement IDs are retained; EDP-001–012 is added. This document does not itself launch the platform, buy subscriptions or book services.

Sources and verification notes · quality
S18  OpenAI: API data controls
https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data
Assess endpoint-specific retention, account eligibility and geography; do not assume zero retention or uniform treatment across endpoints.
S19  OWASP: Application Security Verification Standard
https://asvs.owasp.org/
Security verification baseline. Level 2 is a proposed Valo target, not a certification claim.
S20  W3C: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2
https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/
Accessibility reference. AA is the proposed release target; automated checks alone do not establish conformance.
S21  pg-boss: maintained PostgreSQL job queue
https://github.com/timgit/pg-boss

S22  docx: JavaScript document-generation library
https://docx.js.org/
Candidate DOCX renderer. Compatibility and layout are acceptance-test obligations, not assumed guarantees.
S23  Playwright: Page API and PDF generation
https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-pdf
Reference for PDF export and browser-based testing. Browser binaries and resource limits need production-worker validation.
S24  NIST Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework Generative AI Profile
https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.600-1.pdf
Voluntary risk guidance on confabulation, information integrity, provenance and evaluation. Supports the AI risk controls; not Nigerian law or approval of automated legal publishing. Checked 13 November 2026.
Research boundary
This is an implementation specification, not a legal opinion or audit of the Valo deployment. The S01–S23 retrieval notes are retained from the supplied baseline; they do not validate every state/LGA rule or imply new professional review. S24 informs the AI controls. Production claims still need their own current evidence.
Before production, recheck vendor documentation, account entitlements and software versions, and obtain authoritative text for each published regulatory rule. A regulator logo, search snippet or accessible old page does not establish currency. AI review reduces some errors but cannot certify accuracy, completeness, enforceability or compliance.
